name: Haiku global diversification via US-listed ADRs and ETFs
strategy: Harvest dividend carry from resilient energy and healthcare sectors while reducing rate-sensitive financial exposure; reinforce international diversification through Japan strength; raise cash for post-FOMC optionality
reassessment_note: FOMC rate hike now 60-80% likely as of 2026-09-15. Prior book was over-allocated to rate-sensitive sectors (XLF 15%, KRE 9%, TLT 5% = 29% duration risk) with insufficient hedges and only 13% cash before binary event. Energy (XLE +3.12%) and Japan (EWJ +2.25%) are showing relative strength worthy of reallocation. Trimmed high-beta rate-sensitive positions (financials from 15%→11%, regional banks 9%→6%, bonds 5%→1%) and redirected capital to defensive energy (maintained at 14%), healthcare (maintained at 13%), and international diversification (EWJ 8%→11%, EFA 11%→10%). Raised cash from 13%→25% to preserve flexibility for post-FOMC mean-reversion trades and to reduce leverage exposure in rate-vulnerable book. Dividend yield thesis remains valid; repositioning de-risks rate duration exposure while maintaining income generation from energy and healthcare carry.

positions.thesis: Energy sector has proven resilient (+3.12% in position) as supply-chain shocks from Iran conflict sustain oil prices, providing inflation hedge and dividend yield. Maintained allocation recognizes energy as defensive in rate-hiking cycle while benefiting from geopolitical tailwinds.

Healthcare maintains defensive characteristics and stable dividend yield regardless of rate environment. Slight trim from 14% to 13% reflects reduced need for full defensive weighting given cash buffer increase, but position size sufficient to anchor income generation.

Japan showing relative strength (+2.25% performance) driven by fiscal stimulus and corporate reform (Sanaenomics). Increased from 8% to 11% to capture regional momentum and provide diversification away from US rate-sensitive sectors. Japanese dividend yield attractive and benefits from yen weakness potential.

Value factor continues to offer yield and downside protection in rate-hiking cycle. Slight trim from 11% to 10% to fund rate-risk reduction elsewhere while maintaining value discipline in portfolio construction.

Developed international diversification provides geographic hedge to US rate policy. Slight trim from 11% to 10% reflects concentration reduction but maintains meaningful international diversification in face of US-centric FOMC tightening.

Significant trim from 15% to 11% reflects vulnerability of financial sector to rising rates. Higher rates compress net interest margins (NIM) pressure and multiples; lower allocation preserves some dividend carry while substantially reducing duration risk. Position size scaled to sector exposure rather than income concentration.

Regional bank ETF heavily trimmed from 9% to 6% as rising rates pressure small-cap bank valuations and loan growth. Retained small allocation for sector diversification and because regional bank dividend yields are attractive on dislocation, but sized conservatively given macro headwinds.

Bond ETF dramatically reduced from 5% to 1% as FOMC rate hikes will extend duration losses and reduce carrying yield. Minimal position retained only to maintain ballast concept from original strategy; substantial trim redirects capital from negative-convexity exposure into cash flexibility.
